To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The flip count and nodality are invariant under the action of the automorphism group of a graph; (2) The flip count of a graph can be determined by the flip count of its quotient graph, which in turn can be determined by its eigenvalues; and (3) The flip counts of a graph and its quotient graph are equal, provided that the quotient graph has no multiple edges.
the flip and nodal counting methods are not sufficient in order to resolve the Laplace spectrum of graphs.
the flip counts and nodals counts of isospectral graphs are not sufficient to determine the graph uniquely.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: Given an isospectral pair of graphs, what additional information is required to resolve them?
the following questions: (1) What is the minimal information required to distinguish between isospectral graphs, and (2) how do we construct such examples?
two questions: (1) Can we find examples of isospectral graphs (discrete or quantum) with the same flip or nodal count?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the flip count and nodals count are not enough to distinguish isospectral graphs.
isospectral graphs which share the flip count and nodals count are in fact isomorphic, and hence isospectral graphs are not resolved by either the flip count or the nodal count.
isospectral discrete and isospectral quantum graphs with the identical nodal count and flip count are necessarily isomorphic.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for a given graph G, we construct another graph G' such that the Laplace spectrum of G and G' coincide, the nodal count of G and G', as well as their flip count, are identical.

, in addition to the Laplace spectrum, the flip count and nodality of the eigenfunctions of the Laplacian, we can also use the flip count and the nodal count of the eigenfunctions for the quantum graph Hamiltonian to resolve isospectrality.
the flip count is not sufficient to distinguish discrete and quantum isometric graphs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for both discrete and quantum graphs, the flip count and nodals count are not sufficient to resolve isospectrality.
isospectral graphs can share the same nodal and flip count without sharing any of the eigenfunctions.
, in the discrete and quantum setting, isospectral graphs that are distinguished by the number of nodals and flip count can be systematically produced.
